Trim CRWV after its parabolic run, and hold NBIS for AI-cloud upside. Prioritize US-exposed hardware over ID software names this cycle.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: US IRA domestic-content rules and tariff exemptions are structurally favoring US-based module and inverter makers over Asian importers, a durable margin tailwind.
AI data-center load growth is creating a multi-year baseload demand shock that lifts both solar generation and storage economics globally.
Indonesia's energy transition hinges on nickel-based battery supply chains and EV bus adoption (VKTR), but policy execution and local content rules remain the binding constraint.
sectors.ai: Buy dips in US-listed solar equipment names (FSLR, SEDG, ARRY) as tariff clarity and AI-driven power demand re-rate the group; Indonesia's VKTR upside is real but liquidity-thin, so size small. Rotate from pure-play EPC to vertically integrated manufacturers with US content. Watch VST as a proxy for merchant power pricing.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Small-cap FMCG names are driving outsized returns on low float and retail speculation, a pattern that persists into Indonesia's year-end window but demands tight risk control.
Domestic consumption resilience underpins FMCG demand, yet margin pressure from input costs and logistics keeps aggregate upside capped, favoring niche players over large caps.
Foreign and local institutional flows remain selective, concentrating in names with clear earnings revisions or new product launches, creating sharp divergence within the sector.
sectors.ai: Buy selective small-cap FMCG names with confirmed volume and earnings catalysts (ENZO, PADA, MBTO) into year-end; the broad sector is range-bound, so rotate out of laggards like AGAR and UDNG into leaders with momentum. Position for a 2-3 week squeeze, but trim into any 15%+ extension as liquidity thins into holidays.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's 17,000-island geography structurally underpins multimodal logistics demand, insulating ports and shipping operators from domestic consumption volatility.
Government push on downstream mineral processing and new capital city Nusantara creates recurring heavy-lift and cold-chain infrastructure contracts for listed logistics players.
Digitalization of SME freight and last-mile delivery is compressing margins for pure asset-light brokers, favoring integrated asset owners like ASSA and BULL with pricing power.
sectors.ai: Buy selective logistics names on archipelago-driven structural demand; GTSI, SDMU, and HUMI lead momentum with volume confirmation. Favor operators with port/warehouse assets over pure freight forwarders. Trim exposure if IDX logistics breadth fades below 50% advancing names. Watch US rate signals for second-half capex cycle inflection.

sectors.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
themes: Indonesia's crypto adoption is structurally tied to remittance and cross-border payment corridors, favoring scalable layer-1s like Stellar and Algorand over speculative tokens.
Regulatory clarity under Bappebti and the upcoming OJK transition will increasingly reward compliant, utility-driven assets, compressing meme-coin premiums.
Global institutional staking flows into proof-of-stake networks (ATOM, AVAX, ADA) are a durable driver, as yield demand outpaces retail trading volume in emerging markets.
sectors.ai: Rotate into layer-1s with proven staking yield and Indonesia-accessible liquidity—ALGO, ATOM, AVAX lead momentum and offer real on-chain activity versus meme-driven pumps. Take partial profits on PUMP and HYPE, which are sentiment-exposed and vulnerable to local exchange listing gaps. Rebalance toward ADA and DOT for relative safety, and watch for a pullback to add AVAX below $30.
